transcript.text: hotpoint SA2 oven not heatin on fan, grill ok. wat does SA2 mean??

“SA2” is a Hotpoint oven series/range prefix, not an error code. It is not enough to identify the exact version or a compatible part. With the grill working but the fan oven not heating, the most likely cause is the fan-oven ring element at the back of the oven, or its wiring. The function selector, thermostat/control path, or a clock left in AUTO after a power cut can give a similar symptom. It is not usually the fan motor if the fan is turning. 1. Set the oven to the fan-oven heating symbol (fan inside a circle), set 180°C, and leave it for 10–15 minutes. Make sure it is not on defrost, which runs the fan without heat. Check whether the temperature indicator comes on.
2. Look through the door: is the cavity fan spinning? If it spins but the oven remains cold, the rear fan-oven element becomes the leading suspect, though an engineer would also check its connectors and the control/switch path.
3. Check the clock display. If it is flashing or shows AUTO, set the time and return it to manual mode first; some ovens inhibit heating while timed/automatic mode is set. If it is still cold with the fan running and the clock in manual mode, isolate/unplug the oven before any further inspection. This is normally an engineer repair unless you are confident with appliance electrical work, as access involves internal wiring and mains components.
ok tried fan setting, fan at the back is not spinning, just a low hum. clock is on manual. it barely warms up

The low hum with the cavity fan not turning makes the fan motor the leading fault. It is receiving some power and trying to start, but is either seized/failed or the blade is being held up by an obstruction or rubbing on the rear guard. The clock setting is not the cause. The weak warmth may simply be heat from the fan-oven element without any air circulation, but the element and its wiring cannot be confirmed from that alone. 1. Let the oven go fully cold, then switch it off and isolate/unplug it.
2. Without removing any covers, look through the rear fan guard for anything caught around the blade, or a blade that looks bent and touching the guard. - Something visibly fouling it: that may be the cause. - Nothing visible: a failed/seized cavity fan motor is most likely. Do not use the fan-oven function while the fan is only humming and not turning. This is normally an engineer repair, as confirming the motor versus its wiring requires internal access and electrical testing. The engineer should also check that the fan-oven element is heating properly once the fan fault is dealt with.
isolated it at the cooker switch and let it cool. cant see anything stuck thru the guard tbh. there was a slight hot smell from the back once but not now. so is it the fan motor?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Yes — the cavity fan motor is the most likely fault. A low hum with no rotation usually means the motor is being powered but cannot start, commonly because it has seized or its start winding has failed. As no obstruction is visible through the guard, that makes a simple blockage less likely. A blade rubbing on the rear cover is still possible, but less likely without visible contact or scraping. Do not use the oven again until it has been checked by a qualified appliance engineer. They should confirm the fan motor and blade can turn freely with the supply isolated, then inspect the motor connections and test the motor circuit.
